speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: Okay, I think we've got everyone. Paris, thanks for making time on a Friday afternoon. I'm Benvolio, product at Montague, you've met Juliet, and this is Romeo, who built most of what you're about to see.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: Happy to be here. Juliet said there'd be a tablet in airplane mode, so I'm curious.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: There will be, I promise. So the plan is about twenty minutes. Romeo shows an inspection that's done offline and then syncs. Juliet shows you the signed report. Then we talk about what a pilot looks like. Sound okay?

speaker: Paris Duke
text: Sounds good.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Great. So, I'm sharing my screen, and this is a regular tablet running the Balcony App. And, see up top, it's in airplane mode. No Wi-Fi, no cell. Pretend I'm out in one of your yards, behind a row of trailers.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: That's most of our yards, honestly.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Right, that's what Juliet said. So I'm starting a dock inspection. Site, inspector, I'll take a couple of photos of, um, my desk, which is standing in for a dock door. One finding, door seal damaged. And I sign it.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Now, this little line at the bottom. It says one inspection queued. That's not a spinner, it's a count. It's sitting in a local queue on the tablet, and it'll stay there as long as it needs to.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: And if the inspector does ten of these before they get signal?

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Then it says ten queued. We tested a lot more than ten this week. Tybalt on Juliet's team left three tablets in airplane mode overnight. Okay, so now I'm walking back to the office, and I turn airplane mode off.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: And... there. Queued goes to zero, and the inspection shows as sent. On our side, Mesh Routing picked it up as an event, so it's routed in a couple of seconds, not in a nightly batch.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: Huh. Okay. That's quicker than I expected.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: And that's the part your auditors care about, I think. So let me share mine. This is the signed PDF for the inspection Romeo just did. It's generated as soon as it syncs.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: You've got the site, the inspector, the time it was signed, the photos, the finding. And the signature's at the bottom, with the time it was actually signed out in the yard, not the time it synced.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: Oh, that's important. That was going to be my question. Because if it's signed at six and syncs at eight, the auditor needs to see six.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Exactly. So with the twenty-four-hour window you mentioned Wednesday, the clock starts when your inspector signs.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: Good. That's really good. So, two out of my three. What about the export, by site, into our freight system?

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: That's the honest gap. Export by site is next sprint. We didn't want to fake it for a demo.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: I appreciate that, actually. I'd rather hear next sprint than see something that falls over in March.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: And just to repeat what I said on Wednesday, the data that flows through is your inspections. You see what you send, and nobody's handing you, or anybody, Montague's routing data.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: Yep, I remember. Okay. So what would a pilot look like?

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: We were thinking small. Four weeks, two sites. Pick the two where connectivity is worst, so we really learn something.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: Um, I can do that. I'd want to start on a Monday. March second?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: March second works for us. Export by site is next sprint. We'll confirm timing early next week, and the goal is to have it before your inspectors start.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Yeah, that's comfortable for us.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: Okay then. Four weeks, two sites, starting March second. Let's do it. I'll pick the sites and send them over to Juliet.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: Fantastic. Thank you, Paris. We'll send a short summary today.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: One thing, so nobody's surprised if I'm slow to reply. I'm at a conference in Denver all next week, so I'll be on my phone mostly.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Oh, Denver, nice. Well, that's our neck of the woods, so if you want a coffee, just say.

speaker: Paris Duke
text: I might take you up on that. Thanks, everyone. Good demo.
